answer:
FINAL RESULT — executed DE analysis + documented GSEA-library unavailability + single best-supported pathway.

EXECUTED (real, evidence-backed): The full pipeline ran end-to-end on data/count.csv (21,884 Ensembl-mouse genes; KL1-3 = UBE2M KD, WL1-3 = control, per your lock-in): DESeq2-style median-of-ratios normalization (size factors 1.044/1.052/0.822/1.041/1.090/1.020) → per-gene NB-GLM Wald test with DESeq2-style dispersion-trend shrinkage (MLE cross-check 1.95e-14) → apeglm-equivalent log2FC shrinkage (MLE prior mu=-0.0004, s=0.7107) → DEG filter (p<0.05, |log2FC|>1, baseMean>10). Result: 1,013 DEGs in the KD model (621 up / 392 down); 3,607 genes with raw p<0.05; top up-genes to shrunken log2FC 5.49 (raw 8.18), top down to -3.35. The full 21,884-gene GSEA ranking by shrunken log2FC is saved. A faithful from-scratch classic GSEA engine (running-sum ES / sqrt(p(1-p)), NES, FDR q from 1000 gene-label permutations) was validated on a synthetic case (TRUE_PATHWAY ranked 1st, NES 6.92).

OFFICIAL-LIBRARY GSEA: NOT AVAILABLE — stated plainly, not presented as executed. I made the concrete documented effort you required: (1) final-run re-probe for network + gseapy.get_library('KEGG_2019_Mouse') — no DNS resolution for pypi.org/ensembl/kegg.jp/gseapy.github.io and `import gseapy` → ModuleNotFoundError (logged inside the executed script); (2) full-filesystem re-search including every one of the 11 reachable NFS mount points (the actor dir, the .actor-venv, and the uv-Python stdlib tree) — no cached GMT, no gseapy data dir, no Ensembl→Entrez table anywhere (only 'kegg' hits on disk are task.json and my own script); (3) no new network paths, no privileges to mount additional NFS exports, no reachable gene-set server. Therefore no NES/FDR from the official KEGG_2019_Mouse library can be produced in this environment, and the Ensembl→Entrez mapping the library requires is likewise unreachable.

SINGLE MOST-SUPPORTED PATHWAY (inference, clearly NOT an executed GSEA): "cell cycle" (mmu04110). Rationale: the DEG profile is a broad, strong UP-regulation response (621:392, median up log2FC 1.42, many 10-90-fold inductions of highly expressed genes) — the signature of DNA-damage/replication stress and cell-cycle arrest after loss of the K63-ubiquitin E2 UBE2M/UBC13 — and "cell cycle" is the largest, most GSEA-sensitive KEGG pathway for exactly that signature. Close alternatives if the official library is later run: "p53 signaling pathway" (mmu04115), "DNA replication" (mmu03030), "ubiquitin mediated proteolysis" (mmu04120).

To obtain the definitive gseapy/NES/FDR answer, re-run analysis.py in a networked runner: it auto-detects gseapy + KEGG_2019_Mouse and will use the real library on the saved ranking.

EVIDENCE ARTIFACTS: analysis.py (executed script incl. final-run probe log), deseq2_results.csv (per-gene baseMean/log2FC/p/DEG), gsea_ranking.csv (full-gene shrunken-log2FC ranking).
